history.sg_progress: The Department of Economic and Social Affairs has begun to implement the recommendation. Beginning with the 2021 budget, 2 per cent is allocated to programme level evaluations, which allows for the recruitment of external evaluation consultants. These evaluations are of a complex nature and will require four to six specialists who need to be managed and coordinated. The proposed programme budget for 2022 includes a P-4 post for evaluation under the United Nations Development Account. The Department of Economic and Social Affairs notes that this post will be essential for the coordination and management of these complex evaluations and will ensure the implementation of the recommendation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration ensure that sufficient resources are allocated for conducting the programmatic evaluation in a timely manner.
history.administration_response: The proposed programme budget for 2022 included provision for a temporary P-4 post for evaluation, to be funded from section 35 (Development Account) (A/76/6 (Sect. 35), para. 35.24), which was approved by the General Assembly. While this post is very helpful for conducting programmatic evaluations in the short term, it is important that a permanent post be established, as was done for the three programmatic and management posts within the budget of the Department of Economic and Social Affairs.
history.board_assessment: Given that further review of the resources allocated for conducting the programmatic evaluation is needed, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.sg_progress: Evaluation continues to be a crucial part of the programming of the Development Account. The temporary position of an Evaluation Officer (P-4) under section 35 has been essential to plan the programme-level evaluation of the Account’s response to COVID-19, provide guidance and support to project evaluations and distil lessons learned. The Department will review the continuing need for the post in 2023 and consider a proposal for the 2024 proposed programme budget.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration ensure that sufficient resources are allocated for conducting the programmatic evaluation in a timely manner.
history.administration_response: The proposed conversion of the Evaluation Officer (P-4) post to an established post has been approved by the General Assembly in its resolution 78/252 on the programme budget for 2024. Approximately 4 per cent of the Development Account’s budget ($636,700) is set aside for project- and programme-level evaluations and relevant activities as reflected in the Account’s proposed programme budget for 2024 (A/78/6 (Sect. 35), para. 35.16). The recommendation has been fully implemented. The Administration requests its closure.
history.board_assessment: Given that the resources for project and programme-level evaluations and relevant activities have been allocated, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
